title: Apple Watch Series 11 breathing-disturbance notifications send a 79-year-old to his cardiologist; morning watch ECGs show AF after “elevated” nights and CPAP starts without polysomnography
summary: Fukuoka case (Cureus, 26 May 2026): sleep-apnoea notifications prompted consultation; watch ECGs showed AF only after “elevated” breathing-disturbance nights; CPAP under way, no polysomnography.
account: Maruyama (Haradoi Hospital, Fukuoka), Hieda and Fukata reported in Cureus on 26 May 2026 (publication date used; the consultation is undated) a 79-year-old Japanese man with hypertension, dyslipidaemia, type 2 diabetes and symptomatic paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented by 12-lead ECG a decade earlier. After retirement no paroxysms were documented by ambulatory or standard ECG and pulsed-field ablation was deferred. Some months after he began wearing an Apple Watch Series 11 paired with an iPhone 15 Pro, he consulted the authors about notifications of nocturnal “respiratory disturbance”. He activated the watch ECG every morning and evening; AF paroxysms were detected repeatedly on mornings after nights the watch rated breathing disturbance “elevated” but not after “not elevated” nights, and they terminated by evening. He is undergoing CPAP therapy, and pulsed-field ablation will be considered depending on its effect on the paroxysms. No polysomnography was performed; the authors state that watch-detected breathing disturbance is not equivalent to the apnoea-hypopnoea index, that the watch ECG cannot fully substitute for conventional ECG, and that the notification algorithm “was reportedly developed using advanced machine learning”. The FDA cleared Apple's Sleep Apnea Notification Feature under 510(k) K240929 on 13 September 2024; the 510(k) summary says it uses a deep learning algorithm on Apple Watch accelerometer data, analyzed in 30-day windows, trained on over 11,000 nights with polysomnography or home sleep-test reference. No treatment outcome is reported.
purpose: The notification feature is built to identify patterns of breathing disturbance suggestive of moderate-to-severe sleep apnoea and tell the user; the ECG app is built to record and classify single-lead rhythm; both were used as designed.
system: Apple Watch Sleep Apnea Notification Feature (breathing-disturbance notifications) and the ECG app
model_version: Apple Watch Series 11 with iPhone 15 Pro

ratings.reason: A man whose AF was thought quiescent learned that paroxysms recur after disturbed-breathing nights and started CPAP; no confirmed sleep-apnoea diagnosis and no treatment effect are reported.

ai_role.statement: The notification feature's deep-learning model (per the FDA summary) flagged elevated breathing disturbance and brought the patient to the clinic; his own morning ECG recordings, read by the authors, showed the AF paroxysms, and the paper does not state separately what the ECG app's classifier reported. Clinicians chose CPAP and deferred ablation. The maker's account was not used; the FDA 510(k) summary and one independent case report are the sources.

evidence.title: 510(k) Summary K240929: Sleep Apnea Notification Feature (SANF)
evidence.quote: Breathing disturbance data is analyzed in discrete, consecutive 30-day evaluation windows. If patterns consistent with moderate-to-severe sleep apnea are identified within the 30-day evaluation window, the user is notified.

produced_by: Nightly watch wear with the sleep-apnoea notification feature active, plus the owner's habit of recording a watch ECG every morning and evening
A known history of paroxysmal AF that made the morning traces interpretable to his cardiologists
Access to a clinic willing to act on watch data (CPAP started without polysomnography)
must_hold: The user completes onboarding and wears the watch during sleep, since the feature evaluates 30-day windows opportunistically
Clinicians confirm with conventional ECG and polysomnography, which the authors say the watch cannot replace and which was not done here

headline: Apple Watch breathing alerts send a 79-year-old to CPAP therapy

comparator.against: ambulatory monitoring and standard 12-lead ECG, which had documented no paroxysms since his retirement
comparator.before: AF paroxysms were not documented by ambulatory monitoring or standard ECG
comparator.after: AF paroxysms were detected repeatedly in the morning after notification of nocturnal “elevated” breathing disturbance, but not in the morning after nights when breathing disturbance was “not elevated”
comparator.quote: AF paroxysms were not documented by ambulatory monitoring or standard ECG (Figure 1B), and we deferred pulsed-field ablation for his AF paroxysms.

later.note: The May 2026 report says CPAP therapy is under way and ablation will depend on its effect; no later outcome was found.
